course_name_original: MACHINE DESIGN AND FINITE ELEMENT METHOD
course_name_en: Machine Design and Finite Element Method
prerequisites: Mathematical background (differential equations, integral calculus and matrix algebra)

learning_outcomes.text: Learn the design aspects of mechanical components, with particular reference to the metallic material resistance, in order to assess the component sizing and make a failure diagnosis.
Gain knowledge on low cycle uniaxial fatigue, high cycle multiaxial fatigue, fracture mechanics, plasticity and creep.
Learn how to leverage numerical tools for stress analysis calculations with particular reference to the Finite Element Method (FEM).

syllabus_topics: Multiaxial fatigue: critical plane and energetic approaches
Static and fatigue crack propagation models
Introduction to the Boundary Element Method (BEM) with reference to potential and elastostatic problems
FEM (analytical background, governing equations, type of elements, software development and validation) applications
teaching_methods: Test cases to be solved by groups of students
assessment_rules: To pass the exam, students must recall fundamental concepts of linear elasticity and fatigue, successfully solve written problems, and present a well-structured FEM project. To achieve the highest marks, a deep comprehension of advanced concepts in machine design theory and FEM theory is required. Knowledge of seminar content is only needed to achieve the cum laude mark.
bibliography: L. VERGANI, MECCANICA DEI MATERIALI, MCGRAW-HILL. (From this book the student can study: plasticity, fracture mechanics, low cycle uniaxial fatigue).

P. DAVOLI, A. BERNASCONI, M. FILIPPINI, S. FOLETTI, COMPORTAMENTO MECCANICO DEI MATERIALI, MCGRAW-HILL. (From this book the student can study: plasticity, in addition to what available in the book N.1, high cycle multiaxial fatigue).

G. BELLONI, A. LO CONTE, COSTRUZIONE DI MACCHINE (RESISTENZA DEI MATERIALI E SICUREZZA), HOEPLI. (From this book the student can study: fracture mechanics in addition to what available from book N.1, creep).
G. BELINGARDI, IL METODO DEGLI ELEMENTI FINITI NELLA PROGETTAZIONE MECCANICA, LIBRERIA EDITRICE UNIVERSITARIA, LEVROTTO E BELLA, TORINO.
